mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the last two weeks will continue to depress discretionary shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will remain lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay at or below the current week and RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above its current level while TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed, home-centered behavior substitutes for retail outings and pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases by at least 2 points week-on-week while TRANSIT stays below -70
failure_condition: If the trigger condition occurs and RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior two-week mean within 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further weekly drop in PARKS indicates weaker leisure mobility overall, and that spillover will reduce retail-and-recreation visits in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls week-on-week by at least 5 points
failure_condition: If PARKS falls by 5 or more points and RETAIL_REC does not decline in the next weekly mean, reject the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals renewed access frictions or voluntary avoidance, which will compress retail trips over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -75 and WORKPLACES falls below -45
failure_condition: If both thresholds are crossed and RETAIL_REC is not lower than its last-4-week mean over the following month, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM can substitute for retail shopping trips when households consolidate errands, so a continued increase in grocery visits should pull RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues rising but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to its prior two-week average within 14 days, reject the claim.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with milder home-stay pressure from RESIDENTIAL suggests warmer outdoor substitution that can lift discretionary retail visits after about four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL stops increasing
failure_condition: If PARKS rebounds for two weeks and RESIDENTIAL flattens but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a steep mobility contraction, the simultaneous decline in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT leads consumers to cancel discretionary stops first, so retail mobility will fall further within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops below -40 and TRANSIT drops below -75
failure_condition: If the threshold pair occurs and RETAIL_REC does not worsen in the next weekly observation, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When retail mobility is already weak and workplace mobility keeps falling, compliance or caution effects should propagate into consumer activity and keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC is below -50 and WORKPLACES is below -40
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC is already below -50 with WORKPLACES below -40 but the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than the last 28-day mean, the mechanism fails.
